name: Poets of the World
description: Three thousand years of verse from Greece, Persia, China, Japan, India, the Americas and Europe: the poets whose lines are still learned by heart.

checkpoints.name: Ancient voices
checkpoints.note: Homer sings of war and wandering, Sappho of desire, and Rome's Virgil and Ovid turn the Greek tradition into Latin verse.

checkpoints.name: The medieval masters
checkpoints.note: Tang poets Li Bai and Du Fu, Persia's Ferdowsi, Khayyam, Rumi and Hafez, Japan's Murasaki, and Dante and Chaucer in Europe make poetry of faith, love and the world.

checkpoints.name: Early modern and Romantic
checkpoints.note: Shakespeare turns verse into drama, Bashō shrinks it to seventeen syllables, and Goethe and Pushkin carry a national language into the age of Romanticism.

checkpoints.name: Modern voices
checkpoints.note: Whitman, Dickinson, Tagore, Lorca, Neruda, Szymborska and Angelou write in the new free forms, and Dylan sets the poet's work to a guitar.
